issues.description: Unguarded blocking read loop can hang indefinitely on writer hang or partial crash
issues.detail: After flipping to blocking mode, the inner while-True loop has no timeout and no process-exit check. The original code's bounded-wait and subprocess-failure invariants are lost: a writer that opens then hangs will block the parent forever. Retain a backstop (process-exit check or timeout) on the blocking path.

issues.description: fcntl mode-switch lacks error handling and leaks fd state across the function boundary
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can raise OSError, leaving fd in an inconsistent state with no cleanup on the exception path. The fd is caller-owned and passed in, so mutating its flags without restoring them on exit violates the frame property. Wrap in try/except and restore O_NONBLOCK on return.

issues.description: Patch silently deletes the macOS workaround without justifying the regression risk
issues.detail: The removed block existed precisely because POSIX FIFO behavior was not observed on macOS. The commit claims POSIX guarantees solve it, but provides no evidence the new blocking-read path subsumes the old behavior on macOS. Either prove the macOS case is handled or split the patch and keep the workaround.

issues.description: Function contract under failure modes is unstated and silently changed
issues.detail: The old code raised CalledProcessError when content was empty; the new code may return a partial buffer on writer-crash-mid-write because the blocking loop has no abnormal-exit detection. Document preconditions on fifo_fd ownership and postconditions under writer-crash and writer-hang so the contract is explicit.

issues.description: No regression test added for an intermittent race condition fix
issues.detail: Intermittent JSON truncation at ~86KB is exactly the kind of bug that returns after the next refactor. A test that writes a large payload and closes the writer fast would lock in the fix and document the contract.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler reduced to bare pass, dropping has_blocking_error tracking
issues.detail: The previous code tracked has_blocking_error and used content to decide closure semantics. The new pass quietly changes behavior and is largely dead under the new control flow. Either consolidate with the poll-timeout branch or document why both paths exist; cleanup belongs in a separate patch.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is sound — substituting blocking-read EOF for the poll+process-exit oracle is the right shape — but the execution weakens invariants the old code upheld. The unguarded blocking loop can hang indefinitely on a stuck writer, fcntl flag changes lack error handling and leak fd state to the caller, and a macOS-specific workaround was deleted without justification. The function's failure-mode contract is unstated and silently shifted. Fix the error handling, restore a process-exit or timeout backstop on the blocking path, justify the macOS removal, and add a regression test before landing.
